author: reek
body: A revised field's value is hoisted into a let, because __record-set mutates in place and every value must be computed before the first store. That hoist used to swallow the __narrow: the checker suppresses CDX2051 when it can SEE __narrow at the store, and after hoisting it saw a bare name. So the identical assertion passed in a record literal and was rejected in a revised update, and the diagnostic recommended the very thing the author had already written.

author: reek
body: Both forms below assert the same thing about the same value. Both must compile, and both must trap on the same out-of-range value at runtime -- the assertion has to still be an assertion, not merely a way to quiet the checker.

author: reek
body: The counterpart is errors/revised-narrow-absent: without __narrow, the same store is still CDX2051. If that probe ever passes, this fix has turned the hatch into a hole.

author: reek
body: Each line gets its own Reading, and that is not tidiness. revised is a __record-set chain and __record-set mutates in place, returning the same record -- so `let b = make-revised a 7` would leave a and b the same object, and a later revise of b would rewrite what a reads. The first cut of this test threaded one record through all three and printed the last value three times. Same lesson as list-set-at and ttt-copy-squares: a caller that re-reads the old value must not hand its record to a revise.
